hero.filename: View of the Attack Against Fort Washington.jpeg
hero.caption: Contemporaneous view drawn by British officer Thomas Davies of the attack against Fort Washington on November 16, 1776. Shows artillery fire on the fort and redoubts as well as several boats of soldiers in the river. The New Jersey Palisades and the Hudson River are also shown in the background.

A memorial dedicated to the Battle of Fort Washington in Bennett Park in Manhattan, New York City, at the location of the Battle of Fort Washington. Margaret Corbin rose to fame defending this artillery position, firing a cannon in defense of the Battle of Fort Washington.

images.filename: Fort Washington Collegiate Church Parish Hall 06.jpg
images.caption: The Fort Washington Collegiate Church at 470 Fort Washington Avenue on West 181st Street between Fort Washington Avenue and Magaw Place in the Washington Heights neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City was built in 1908-09 and was designed in Nelson & Van Wagenen in the Country Gothic style. It began as an outreach project of the West End Collegiate Church and gained full standing in 1916 as one of the four collegiate churches in Manhattan. It later merged with the Hamilton Grange Reformed Church, and took in members of the Harlem Reformed Dutch Church. The plaque was re-installed following the 2013-2021 restoration.
